payload.selection_rationale:
There was one proposal (practice), and it is selected as the core. The reason is that the measurements support it, not that it reads well.

What the build check and spikes measured at HEAD bd6572f:
- The survey measured the whole tool chain on bounded roots: 964/964 tests, 21/21 W-001 tests, and three W-001 runs PASSED with verdict held.
- Spike 1 ran the whole-drive branch of Test-W001 on D:\ and on a subst T:\ and found it held: the wcifs check, CheckPanelAgrees under whole-drive scope, and Write-W001Record.
- Spike 2 measured a cold app scan of C:\Windows at 71.8 s, which projects to about 468 s for the whole drive against the 1,200 s wait.
- Spike 3 put a code-1920 row through every W-001 check and still got verdict held.

So nothing in the code stands between the person and the run. The slice's real deliverable is a person's run plus a committed counts-only record. Lesson #425 (record plus recipe) and the practice designer's over_engineering_flag both point the same way, and the flag is honoured: no wrapper script, no Sandbox stand-in, no separate judging script, no Core or report change.

Checked against the tree:
- Test-W001 at WindowCases.ps1:6202-6303 does what the proposal says. That covers the whole-drive test at 6210, the 1,200 s rows-mode wait at 6220, the early return with no record when no report exists at 6226, the precaution check at 6228-6231 and the C:-only record path at 6293.
- RowsMode.cs:18 states that rows mode has no deadline of its own. The 120 s ending deadline that lesson #174 hit is TreeMode.cs:73.
- Get-HeaderCount at 5431 matches the header as a prefix ('^Unreadable folders \(...\)'), so the whole drive's header 'Unreadable folders (N), not scanned (1)' (the X-004 shape) still yields N.

One piece of the proposal is a correction the brief needed. Criterion 5's 682-684 came from scans that entered the container layer store (U-112's failed-row groups include Containers\Layers paths). The run the slice specifies leaves the store out. So the figure cannot be reproduced, and criterion 5 is judged as a reconciliation, with each difference named.

components.name: Hand-off doc
components.responsibility:
The person's one page, in six parts.
(1) Pre-flight:
- an unelevated pwsh 7 window, not cmd.exe
- the working directory is the SL-107 worktree
- no TAAD engine stage and no other WindowCases, RuleCases or Mutants run in progress
- heavy apps closed
- the app window left alone for up to 20 minutes (5-10 expected)
- a warning that kernel pool may grow by about 537 MB or more (SL-095; lesson #348 says a cold full scan may cost several GiB) and may not come back before a restart.
(2) The command, with the console teed: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 -Root C:\ 2>&1 | Tee-Object -FilePath artifacts\c-drive-console.txt`.
(3) A table of endings, each keyed by the last printed line, with what to do after each: PASSED, FAILED with a record, FAILED with no record (TIMEOUT, or the cmd.exe 'is not a folder' form), INCONCLUSIVE, and a stopped or closed app.
(4) Which record fields settle criteria 1-4.
(5) The criterion-5 reconciliation table, with the measured subtotals at HEAD: C:\Windows 52 rows (spike 2), WER 438 (survey), fsa-guard-tests 27 code 363 (survey), and W-001's own control-denied +1.
(6) SC-136's corrected expectations, and what to commit.
components.key_interactions: Points at the command in SL-089-seams.md. Names Test-W001's endings and the record's fields exactly as WindowCases.ps1 writes them, including byKind.openedNothingListed, which SL-106 added. Tells the person to copy any 'LEAK:' path into a note kept outside git, and that the fix for a leak starts by extending W001OracleCorpus.json (lesson #361).

components.name: SL-089 seams amendment
components.responsibility: Two sentences under 'Criterion 3 on C:\ is a person's run', next to the command at line 53. First: run it from pwsh with `-Root C:\`; typed in cmd.exe, `-Root "C:\"` arrives as `C:"` and W-001 stops with 'is not a folder', exit 1, nothing written. Second: a pointer to docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md for the expected counts and the endings.
components.key_interactions: The slice text sends the person to this doc for the command, so the hazard has to be written where the command is read (the survey found that only the slice text carried it).

components.name: W-001 whole-drive run (existing, unchanged)
components.responsibility:
Test-W001 runs as it is. In order:
- it refuses to run elevated
- it plants the checker controls under GetTempPath()\fsa-window-cases\<guid>
- it scans C:\ in rows mode under a 1,200 s wait
- it checks that core.status is Completed and that the wcifs-layer-store precaution was on
- it checks rows = header = core.unreadable, no duplicate and no empty reason
- it puts every code-5 NothingListed row to the oracle, and prints 'LEAK:' for any row that opens
- it writes the record to .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json.
components.key_interactions: The chain: Invoke-HookedRun, then Start-App with Format-AppArgument, then the FsaWindowHook rows dump, then Read-RowsDump and CheckPanelAgrees, then Get-OracleRow, then Get-W001Verdict, then Write-W001Record.

components.name: FsaWindowHook rows mode (existing)
components.responsibility: Writes the panel's rows, its notScanned lines and a closing 'rows' line at shutdown. It presses nothing and has no deadline of its own, so a whole drive runs to its ending.
components.key_interactions: Read by Read-RowsDump. The store the precaution left out arrives as one notScanned line, never as a row.

components.name: wcifs-layer-store precaution (existing KnownWorkarounds entry, not changed)
components.responsibility: The one outside-defect workaround this run depends on, a wcifs.sys leak. It is on at every launch: it leaves the container layer store out of a C:\ scan, and the panel says so in a 'not scanned' row and in the tab header (X-002/X-004). This design adds no workaround and no setting.
components.key_interactions: Test-W001 fails a whole-drive run unless the report's workarounds list holds exactly one 'wcifs-layer-store' entry with on=true. The store left out is reconciliation item (a) of criterion 5, and the record's notScanned field (expected 1) is that notice, carried into the record.

components.name: The record
components.responsibility:
The deliverable. Write-W001Record writes it from a run that reached core.status Completed, and it is committed on slice/SL-107. It holds:
- counts
- codes
- panel reasons
- the commit hash
- kernelPoolBytes
- checkerControls
- the verdict.
It holds no path.
components.key_interactions: Read by the person's SC-136/SC-138 check and by SL-107's validate when present. Q-193 (still open) can cite its notScanned, header and kernelPoolBytes. SL-089's own index.json is not edited (Q-106: an export only).

components.name: Console capture
components.responsibility: A gitignored copy of the run's console. It is the only place a leaked row's path survives, because Invoke-WithHook deletes the hook log. It also holds the hook lines, the kernel-pool line and the printed record.
components.key_interactions: Never committed (artifacts/ is in .gitignore). A 'LEAK:' path is copied from it into a bug note outside git.

components.name: Counts-only rule over the committed record
components.responsibility: The architecture rule this design appends (engine-appended, settled, no xUnit twin): the committed c-drive-run.json must not contain a drive-letter path or a 'path' key.
components.key_interactions: It backs Write-W001Record's write-time allow-list once the file is in git, against a hand edit or a later writer. It matches no file until the person commits the record, and the gates treat that as a pass (Q-012).

contracts.name: W-001 whole-drive invocation
contracts.auth_model: The ordinary, unelevated interactive user, from pwsh 7. An elevated token makes Test-W001 return INCONCLUSIVE (exit 3) before anything is scanned.
contracts.error_cases:
- From cmd.exe, `-Root "C:\"` arrives as `C:"`. It throws 'W-001: C:" is not a folder': FAILED, exit 1, no record.
- The app still running at 1,200 s: Wait-App kills it and returns 'TIMEOUT'. The exit-code check fails, there is no report, so Test-W001 returns before writing a record: FAILED, exit 1, no record.
- core.status not Completed (the person stopped or closed the app): FAILED, and the record IS written with that status and verdict 'failed'. It must not be committed.
- Any failed check or any leak: FAILED, exit 1, and the record is written with verdict 'failed'.
- A checker control misbehaves: INCONCLUSIVE, exit 3, and the record is written with verdict 'inconclusive'.
- The precaution is off: the wcifs check fails, so FAILED.
contracts.notes: Judge the ending by the last printed line (PASSED: W-001 / FAILED: W-001 / INCONCLUSIVE: W-001), not by the pipeline's exit code, because the Tee-Object wrapper's effect on $LASTEXITCODE was never exercised. A run that writes the record prints `record: <worktree>\.taad\slices\SL-089\c-drive-run.json`. $Repo is the checkout the script runs from, so it has to be run in the SL-107 worktree. `-Root C:` without the backslash also counts as whole-drive (survey). The doc names only `-Root C:\`.

contracts.name: c-drive-run.json
contracts.auth_model: None: a file in the repo. Write-W001Record's allow-list and the counts-only architecture rule keep paths out (Q-016).
contracts.error_cases:
- A string outside the allow-list makes the write throw, and nothing is written.
- A Completed-but-failed run, or a Cancelled run that produced a report, overwrites any earlier file at this path in the working tree. So commit right after a Completed run.
contracts.notes:
Fields read per criterion:
- C1: scope 'whole-drive', elevated false, checkerElevated false, status 'Completed', checkerControls.openable/denied/refusedThenListed all true, verdict 'held'.
- C2: rows == header == coreUnreadable.
- C3: oracle.openRefusedButOpenable 0, and no 'LEAK:' line in artifacts\c-drive-console.txt.
- C4: emptyReasons 0, duplicates 0.
- C5: byCode and oracle.leftoverRows, against the reconciliation table.
Expected alongside:
- notScanned 1 (the store)
- byKind.openedNothingListed 0 and listedPartway 0 (local NTFS; U-098 measured 0 partly listed; lesson #465)
- oracle.leftoverRows.code363 27-28 and reparse 0
- notARefusedKeepShape [] or a code-1920 entry with count 2 or less.
The record holds no count of refused-then-listed folders.

contracts.name: LEAK console line
contracts.error_cases: Lost if the console was not captured: the hook log is deleted in Invoke-WithHook's finally.
contracts.notes: Format: `        LEAK: a row with code 5 that opens: <path>`. It must stay out of git (Q-016).

key_decisions.decision: Change no code. Test-W001, its 1,200 s rows-mode wait and its record format are used exactly as they are at HEAD. The build delivers two docs; the person's run delivers the record.
key_decisions.rationale: The survey measured the chain at HEAD on three bounded roots. Spike 1 ran the whole-drive branch on D:\ and subst T:\ (held). Spike 3 ran a code-1920 row through every check (held). Spike 2 projects a cold C: app run at about 468 s against 1,200 s, and the whole-C: Core scans of U-108/U-110/U-111/U-112 took 159-409 s, with the app adding no overhead over Core when warm. Rows mode has no deadline (RowsMode.cs:18). If the person's run ever times out, raising the literal at WindowCases.ps1:6220 is a one-line follow-up; it is not built speculatively, because touching WindowCases.ps1 makes WindowMutants -Mutant All a required validate check (Q-114).

key_decisions.decision: Nothing in this slice's machine-checked cases waits on the person's run. Criteria 1-5 of the build check stay checked_by person, on the backlog as SC-136/SC-138, and they are not filed again. The cases this design lists are all settled by commands the validator runs unattended: the doc text, the cmd.exe hazard, the whole-drive branch on D:\, the store left out on a bounded root, the fixture leftovers, and the oracle corpus.
key_decisions.rationale: Lesson #357 says to mark a whole-drive criterion checked_by person up front. SL-095 shows the cost of not doing so: a person-run measurement left in the definition of done cost 6 of its 8 builds. The engine's per-run pool guard is not allowed to run a whole-C:\ scan (~537 MB, SL-095).

key_decisions.decision:
Judge criterion 5 as an itemised reconciliation from the measured 682, not against 682-684 raw. Start from 682 = 652 code 5 + 28 code 363 + 2 code 1920 (U-098/U-110/U-112 at 9a7a2c4; U-111's 684 adds 2 transient fixture rows). The items:
(a) The layer store is now not scanned: subtract every row under ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers. That is at least 25 (U-112's groups of 10, 8 and 7); the rest is unmeasured. Expect notScanned = 1.
(b) WER drift: all of WER is 438 now (survey) against ReportArchive alone at 451 (U-112), so about 13 or more fewer.
(c) Code 1920: the stand-in-bin folders are no longer reparse points (spike 3), so 0 is expected, at most 2.
(d) Code 363: 27 under fsa-guard-tests (survey at HEAD), plus fsa-validate-2\dirtag\nonempty if it still exists, so 27-28.
(e) One more code-5 row: W-001's own control-denied under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-window-cases\<guid>, still refused.
(f) Other cases' leftovers under fsa-window-cases (12 in U-112): plus or minus 12, churn.
Measured anchors at HEAD: C:\Windows 52 (spike 2), WER 438, fsa-guard-tests 27.
Result: code 5 at most about 627 (652 minus 25, lower again by the WER drift); rows at most about 660; no hard floor.
key_decisions.rationale: Every C: count behind 682-684 came from Scanner.Scan with the store entered: their failed-row groups include Containers\Layers\...\Files paths. The run this slice must make has the precaution on, so the store is one not-scanned folder (X-002/X-004 shape; SL-089 measured notScanned once on ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows). The brief's figure cannot come out of the run it specifies, so 'near' can only mean 'every difference named'. The hard pass rests on criteria 1-4 and verdict held. If U-110's results\a-c-drive.json still survives in its spike folder, it gives item (a) a floor; lesson #404 says spike folders vanish, so the design does not depend on it.

key_decisions.decision:
Correct SC-136's '~30 leftover rows' to:
- oracle.leftoverRows.code363 27-28
- oracle.leftoverRows.reparse 0
- notARefusedKeepShape [] or a code-1920 entry with count 2 or less.
key_decisions.rationale: Get-OracleRow (6132-6145) tests code 363 first, then any code other than 5, which is 'other-code' and goes into notARefusedKeepShape. Only a code-5 reparse folder is 'leftover-reparse'. So the 1920 rows can never be in leftoverRows. Summing the two buckets as '~30 leftover' would misread a correct record as short. W001OracleCorpus F12 pins 1920 as other-code.

key_decisions.decision: Do not clean the %TEMP% test fixtures (fsa-guard-tests, fsa-window-cases, fsa-validate-2) before the run. Subtract them in the reconciliation instead.
key_decisions.rationale: The 27 code-363 fixture rows are part of criterion 5's expected count, and Q-258 names W-001 over them as the re-check across cldflt builds. Deleting them changes the population being measured and loses the fixtures. Lesson #333's 'subtract or clean' is met by subtraction.

key_decisions.decision: Run from the SL-107 worktree, alone on the machine, with the console teed to gitignored artifacts\c-drive-console.txt. Commit only a record from a run that reached core.status Completed, whether held or failed. A run that timed out, was stopped or was closed is re-run, not committed.
key_decisions.rationale: $Repo is the folder two levels above the script, so the record lands in the checkout that runs it, and its commit field is that HEAD. Test-W001 writes the record even when checks fail, and its allow-list accepts 'Cancelled', so a stopped run would overwrite the path with a record that says nothing about criterion 3. Running alone keeps the scan's pool growth from tripping a concurrent engine stage's guard (lesson #357), and keeps other cases' ACL churn out of the scanned tree.

key_decisions.decision: Do not hand-edit .taad/slices/SL-089/index.json. Criterion 3 of SL-089 is discharged by the committed record and SC-136/SC-138's check of it.
key_decisions.rationale: Q-106: .taad/slices JSON is an export of the engine DB, and nothing reads it back. A hand edit changes nothing and is overwritten on the next refresh.

key_decisions.decision: Leave the ~306,000 refused-then-listed count out of the record. The in-run evidence for criterion 3 is the oracle together with W-001's own control-refused-keep folder: a planted refused-then-listed folder inside the scanned C:\ tree that would print LEAK if the engine ever made it a row. Exposing the count is filed as later work.
key_decisions.rationale: The schema-1 report carries no refused-then-listed count, and LastAccessAsked/Kept are internal to Core (U-102). Exposing them changes the report contract and Core, which is scanner tier, for a context figure. The keep folder is made, and its ACL set, before scanStart, so the oracle cannot exempt it as changed-since-scan. With the store out, the true figure is also below U-108's 306,468, which counted the store's mirrored WinSxS pairs.

key_decisions.decision: Add no workaround and no setting. The run depends on the existing 'wcifs-layer-store' KnownWorkarounds entry (outside defect: the wcifs.sys leak in the Windows container layer filter, out of this product's scope; Q-186). The entry is on by default, has its own checkbox, and turning it off goes through a confirmation that names the consequence. Its notice beside the result already exists: the 'Not scanned, size not counted ... Skipped to avoid a leak in wcifs.sys' note and the tab header's ', not scanned (1)' (X-002). The record carries it as notScanned.
key_decisions.rationale: The defect lives in wcifs.sys, not in this project, and SL-095 built its workaround to the one-entry-per-bug rule. This slice changes neither the precaution nor its notice. The only thing it adds is naming the store left out as reconciliation item (a), where the record's count differs because of it.

key_decisions.decision: Append one architecture rule: the committed .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json must not contain a drive-letter path or a 'path' key.
key_decisions.rationale: This slice is the first to commit a record produced by a run over the person's whole drive. A path in git publishes the person's folder names (Q-016). Write-W001Record refuses a path at write time, but nothing checks the file once committed: a hand edit by the person, or a later writer reusing the path, would pass every gate. As a settled rule it adds no default-suite Fact (lesson #425).

proposals.note:
The only proposal; nobody contested it. Taken whole, with these changes:
- WER item (b) restated: 438 is all of WER, 451 was ReportArchive alone.
- The measured C:\Windows subtotal (52, spike 2) added as an anchor.
- Its code claim that 'C-002 states the store is one not-scanned folder' replaced by X-002/X-004, which are in the tree.
- A counts-only architecture rule over the committed record added.
- An explicit split made between the machine-checked cases and the person-run criteria (SC-136/SC-138), so the definition of done does not wait on the person.
Its over_engineering_flag was honoured: no wrapper, no judging script, no Core or report change.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal, so there is no composition to check. Nothing here has yet survived a disagreement. This design is the first thing anybody has argued with, and the reviewer should treat it that way.

Checks run within the single proposal and against the tree:
1. The proposal reads criterion 1 as needing verdict held, and also says to commit a Completed record even when it failed. These fit together: a failed Completed record is true evidence and leaves criterion 1 unmet. Only records that are not Completed are kept out.
2. Its 'do not clean fixtures' decision against lesson #333's 'subtract or clean' is resolved by subtracting in the reconciliation table.
3. Criterion 3 cites about 306,000 refused-then-listed folders, but the record carries no such count (the schema-1 report has none). The design states this plainly and puts the planted control-refused-keep folder in its place as the in-run tripwire. Get-CheckerControls plants it before scanStart, so the oracle cannot exempt it.
4. It expects notScanned 1 together with header = rows. Get-HeaderCount at WindowCases.ps1:5431 matches '^Unreadable folders \(([\d,]+)\)' as a prefix, so X-004's header 'Unreadable folders (N), not scanned (1)' still yields N. No contradiction.
5. Its leftover arithmetic matches Get-OracleRow's order (363, then any code other than 5, then reparse), checked at 6136-6139.
6. Its WER item mixed populations: 438 is all of WER, 451 was ReportArchive. It was restated as 'about 13 or more fewer'.
7. It cited 'C-002' for the store-left-out shape. The tree's cases for that are X-002/X-004, so those are cited instead.

Added by this composition:
- The counts-only architecture rule.
- The explicit rule that no machine-checked case waits on the person's run.

Reported contradiction, not resolved here: lesson #357 and SL-089-seams.md give the engine's per-run pool guard as 0.5 GB, but the survey reports that its own watch stops at 3 GB of kernel growth. The two are recorded as a decidable disagreement rather than one being picked.

architecture_rules.name: the committed whole-C:\ record carries counts, codes and reasons, never a path
architecture_rules.because: This file is the one record of a scan of the person's whole drive that is committed to git. A path in it, or a dumped row with a 'path' key, publishes the person's folder names (Q-016). Write-W001Record refuses a string with a slash or a backslash only at write time, so a hand edit before the commit, or a later writer reusing this path, would otherwise pass every gate. Patterns widened at build (design review m1) from a drive letter followed by a separator to the writer's own test over the file text: any '/', and any backslash that is not the JSON escape for a quote or a code unit (\" or \uXXXX), and the \u005c and \u002f spellings.

cases.behaviour: hand the person the whole-C:\ command
cases.shape: it is typed in cmd.exe as `-Root "C:\"`
cases.why: In cmd.exe the backslash escapes the closing quote, so the script receives `C:"`. Test-W001 throws at 6204 before any scan, and the runner prints FAILED with exit 1 and writes no record. The doc's warning has to describe what actually happens, and that has so far been measured only through an echo script.
cases.check: From cmd.exe, using a temporary .cmd file that holds the line so that pwsh's own quoting of a cmd argument does not interfere, run: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests\window\WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 -Root "C:\"`. Expect: exit code 1, the output contains `C:" is not a folder` and `FAILED: W-001`, and `Test-Path .taad\slices\SL-089\c-drive-run.json` is False both before and after.

cases.behaviour: hand the person the whole-C:\ command
cases.shape: the person reads only SL-089-seams.md, where the slice text sends them
cases.why: The survey found that seams.md:53 gives the command but says nothing of the cmd.exe hazard. A person who follows only that doc can lose a run.
cases.check: `Select-String -Path docs/design/SL-089-seams.md -Pattern 'cmd\.exe'` and `Select-String -Path docs/design/SL-089-seams.md -SimpleMatch 'SL-107-c-drive-run.md'` each find at least one line under '## Criterion 3 on C:\ is a person's run'.

cases.behaviour: hand the person the whole-C:\ command
cases.shape: the person reads only the SL-107 hand-off doc
cases.why: The doc is the recipe. If it lacks the exact command, the console capture or any of the endings, a run fails or a LEAK path is lost with nothing in the doc to catch it.
cases.check: `Select-String -Path docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md -SimpleMatch` finds each of: `-Case W-001 -Root C:\`, `Tee-Object`, `artifacts\c-drive-console.txt`, `PASSED: W-001`, `FAILED: W-001`, `INCONCLUSIVE: W-001`, `TIMEOUT`, `LEAK:`, `openRefusedButOpenable`, `notScanned` and `leftoverRows`.

cases.behaviour: run W-001 over a whole drive
cases.shape: the root is a whole volume other than C: (D:\)
cases.why: The whole-drive branch has to hold at the slice's final HEAD before a person spends a 10-minute C: run on it: the GetPathRoot test at 6210, the precaution check at 6228-6231 and CheckPanelAgrees under whole-drive scope. A non-C: drive must also not write the C: record path at 6293.
cases.check:
Run alone: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 -Root D:\`. Expect:
- exit 0, with last line `PASSED: W-001`
- a `record:` line naming artifacts\w001-run.json
- in that file: scope 'whole-drive', verdict 'held', rows = header = coreUnreadable
- .taad\slices\SL-089\c-drive-run.json still absent.

cases.behaviour: run W-001 over a tree that holds the container layer store
cases.shape: the precaution is on and the root is above the store (C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows)
cases.why: Reconciliation item (a) depends on the store arriving as one notScanned line and contributing no rows. The header then reads 'Unreadable folders (N), not scanned (1)', and Get-HeaderCount must still yield N, or CheckPanelAgrees fails the whole-C: run.
cases.check: Run alone: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 -Root C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows`. Expect: exit 0, `PASSED: W-001`, and in artifacts\w001-run.json notScanned 1, rows = header = coreUnreadable, oracle.openRefusedButOpenable 0, verdict 'held'.

cases.behaviour: run W-001 over the test fixtures that criterion 5 counts
cases.shape: the folders are stuck cloud placeholders that fail at open with 363 (fsa-guard-tests)
cases.why: SC-136's corrected expectation and item (d) rest on these 27 rows being tallied as leftover-363 and never opened, with no OpenedNothingListed and no 1920 among them.
cases.check: Run alone: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 -Root C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp\fsa-guard-tests`. Expect: exit 0, `PASSED: W-001`, and in artifacts\w001-run.json oracle.leftoverRows.code363 27, leftoverRows.reparse 0, notARefusedKeepShape empty, byKind.openedNothingListed 0, oracle.opened 0.

cases.behaviour: classify a panel row for the record
cases.why: SC-136's '~30 leftover' summed this row into leftoverRows. Get-OracleRow sends it to other-code, and so to notARefusedKeepShape, and the doc's expectation table depends on that.
cases.check: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~W001Oracle"` passes. Corpus row F12 (code 1920) is expected 'other-code'.

cases.behaviour: classify a panel row for the record
cases.shape: a code-5 row whose folder opens (the leak criterion 3 guards against)
cases.why: The doc's endings table says a leak prints 'LEAK:' and gives verdict failed. The corpus is what pins that classification.
cases.check: The same W001Oracle filter passes. Corpus row F02 (code 5, listable) is expected 'leak'.

cases.shape: the app is still running when the 1,200 s wait expires
cases.why: Wait-App kills the app and returns TIMEOUT, so no report exists and Test-W001 returns at 6226 without writing a record. The doc tells the person to re-run.
cases.check: Not run. Exercising it needs a run longer than 20 minutes or a code change. The branch is read in code (Wait-App 479-486, Test-W001 6224-6226), and spike 2 projects a cold run at about 468 s.

cases.why: An elevated token opens folders an ordinary user cannot, so Test-W001 returns INCONCLUSIVE with exit 3 at 6206-6208 before scanning.
cases.check: Not run. It needs an elevated session, which no unattended check has. The code is existing and unchanged.

cases.shape: the wcifs-layer-store precaution is off for the whole drive
cases.why: Test-W001 fails a whole-drive run whose report does not show exactly one 'wcifs-layer-store' entry with on=true (6228-6231).
cases.check: Not run. Off is a session-only GUI toggle behind a confirmation. X-005 already covers the toggle and its question. Turning it off over C:\ would reintroduce the wcifs.sys pool growth the precaution exists to avoid, so this design never asks for that run.

code_claims.claim: Refuses to run elevated (Inconclusive), treats a root equal to its GetPathRoot as whole-drive, and runs the app in hook mode 'rows' with FSA_HOOK_ROWS=1 under a 1,200 s wait.
Test-W001 writes the record to .taad\slices\SL-089\c-drive-run.json only for a whole-drive root starting with C:, and otherwise to artifacts\w001-run.json.
For a whole-drive root, Test-W001 checks that the report's workarounds hold exactly one 'wcifs-layer-store' entry with on true.
Throws 'W-001: <root> is not a folder' when -Root is not an existing folder, and returns before writing any record when no report was written.
Plants control-denied (ListDirectory denied) and control-refused-keep (WriteAttributes denied) in the case folder, and checks that a plain open of the Windows folder succeeds.
Makes the case folder under GetTempPath()\fsa-window-cases\<guid>.
Tallies code 363 as leftover-363, any other non-5 code as other-code, and a code-5 reparse folder as leftover-reparse, all without opening anything; opens only code-5 non-reparse rows.
Throws and writes nothing if any string in the record is not a fixed name (including 'Cancelled'), a 40-hex commit, or a panel reason without a slash or backslash.
Returns 'failed' on any failed check or leak, 'inconclusive' when any of the three checker controls misbehaved, and 'held' otherwise.
Deletes the hook log in its finally block, so a leaked row's path survives only in the console 'LEAK:' line.
Kills the app and returns 'TIMEOUT' when it has not exited within the timeout.
Quotes the path and doubles any trailing backslashes, so C:\ reaches the app intact.
$Repo is the folder two levels above the script's own folder, so the record lands in whichever checkout runs the script.
The run loop prints FAILED and exits 1 on any failure, prints INCONCLUSIVE and exits 3 on any inconclusive check, and otherwise prints PASSED and exits 0.
Matches the visible tab header against '^Unreadable folders \(([\d,]+)\)' as a prefix, so a header ending ', not scanned (1)' still yields N; returns 0 when the tab is not visible.
Fails when there is no closing 'rows' line or it carries an error, then requires dump rows = header N = core.unreadable, no path twice and no blank reason.
Separates the dump's 'row' events from its 'notScanned' events, so the store left out is never counted as a row.
Expects a scan of the store's grandparent to report the header 'Unreadable folders (N), not scanned (1)' and core.skippedStores 1.
Turns the wcifs-layer-store checkbox off through the hook's settings mode and checks that the next launch starts with it on again.
With FSA_HOOK_MODE=rows the hook presses nothing and has no deadline of its own, so the scan runs to whatever ending it reaches.
The 120 s ending deadline is TreeMode's, not part of the rows mode W-001 uses.
Row F12, a code-1920 NothingListed row, is expected 'other-code', and row F02, a code-5 listable row, is expected 'leak'.
The schema-1 report lists every KnownWorkarounds entry by id, with whether it was on.
DefaultEnabled is the set of DefaultOn entry ids, and the file declares the 'wcifs-layer-store' entry.
The window starts every session with KnownWorkarounds.DefaultEnabled, so the precaution is on without the person setting anything.
The store is left out only while the precaution's id is in the enabled set, which defaults to KnownWorkarounds.DefaultEnabled.
Under 'Criterion 3 on C:\ is a person's run' it gives the pwsh W-001 command with -Root C:\ and explains Format-AppArgument's handling of the trailing backslash.
artifacts/ is gitignored, so a console capture written there never reaches a commit.

decidable_disagreements.question: Does the engine guard that applies to an unattended stage stop a run at 0.5 GB of kernel-pool growth, or at 3 GB?
decidable_disagreements.positions:
- 0.5 GB: lesson #357, SL-089-seams.md:47-49 and the Test-W001 comment at 6199-6200 say the per-run guard is 0.5 GB, which a cold C: scan (~537 MB) exceeds.
- 3 GB: the build-check survey reports that the watch it ran under stops at 3 GB.
Both come from the engine. If the 3 GB guard applies to validate and the person grants the allowance the survey said a whole-drive scan needs, the engine's validate could run the whole-C:\ W-001 itself. Criteria 1-5 would then move from a person's run to a machine check of the record. Recorded as a fact, not a design fork (build SL-107, critique m3): older docs (lesson #357, SL-089-seams.md:47-49, the Test-W001 comment at WindowCases.ps1:6199-6200) give 0.5 GB per run; the engine's current watch stops at 3 GB of kernel growth; this slice depends on neither, because the brief names the run the owner's and a cold full scan is predicted at 3-4.4 GiB (lesson #348, Q-188), past either figure.

open_questions: Criterion 5 asks for about 682-684 rows (652/28/2), but those counts were measured with the container layer store scanned. The run the slice requires leaves the store out, and Test-W001 fails a whole-drive run that does not. Does the person accept criterion 5 as met when the record's counts are explained item by item: rows at most about 660, code 363 27-28, code 1920 0-2, notScanned 1, every difference from 682 named? The only like-for-like alternative is a scan with the precaution off, which brings back the wcifs.sys pool growth.
taste_disagreements: Uncontested; one proposal. Where the criterion-5 reconciliation table lives (the new SL-107 doc, or appended to SL-089-seams.md) is a placement choice the reviewer may reverse.

Uncontested; one proposal. Teeing the console into artifacts\ versus asking the person to keep the window's scrollback is a convenience choice. The design picks Tee-Object because the hook log is deleted.

cross_domain_transfer.pattern: An expected balance from an older statement is carried to the new one by listing each reconciling item with its own source. Only the unexplained residual is judged, and 'close enough' is never accepted without that list.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: Criterion 5's expected counts come from scans of a different population: the layer store was entered, the code-1920 fixtures were reparse points, and WER held more reports. Comparing the new record to 682-684 raw would either fail a correct run or pass it on hand-waving. Listing the items makes each difference checkable and leaves only fixture churn to judgement.

invariants.precondition: Every reconciling item has its own measurement or a stated bound.
invariants.evidence: Measured: WER 438 (survey at HEAD), C:\Windows 52 (spike 2), fsa-guard-tests 27 × 363 (survey), and stand-in-bin no longer a reparse point (spike 3). The +1 for the control-denied folder is read from New-CaseFolder and Get-CheckerControls. Bounded below only: the layer-store rows, at least 25 from U-112's top groups.

invariants.precondition: Both statements are put on the same footing before being compared: the old scans entered the layer store and this run does not.
invariants.evidence: X-002/X-004 pin the store as one not-scanned folder with the precaution on. U-112's groups show Containers\Layers rows inside the old 682. Item (a) carries the difference.

invariants.precondition: The reconciliation never stands in for the hard checks.
invariants.evidence: Criteria 1-4 are judged by Test-W001's own checks (CheckPanelAgrees, zero leaks, emptyReasons, duplicates) and by its verdict, whatever the totals are.

prior_art.pattern: Run each acceptance criterion as an external check and record the command, its exit code and an output excerpt for each criterion. A deliverable is judged against its contract, not against a statement.

A scan that swallowed permission errors read a denied root as empty and silently dropped its rows; the fix surfaced the denial. W-001 checks the converse: no folder that was in fact read may appear as a failure.

A runbook with pre-flight conditions, a single command, a table of endings with the action for each, and abort criteria, so that a person's run is repeatable and its failure modes are named in advance.
prior_art.where: SRE runbook / game-day practice (Google SRE book)

prior_art.pattern: Under CommandLineToArgvW's rules, a backslash right before a closing quote escapes the quote. The standard fix is to double trailing backslashes before quoting.
prior_art.where: Microsoft documentation for CommandLineToArgvW / the MSVC argument-parsing rules

prior_art.pattern: Reconcile an expected figure to an observed one by listing each reconciling item, rather than accepting a tolerance.
